questions.answer: Dance classes in Budapest with my favourite dance teachers.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The lectures and classes were super interesting and more practical than in Copenhagen. But the whole application procedure is horribly bureaucratic and is very demotivating.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Everything was a mess and very confusing. Somehow I managed to figure things out, but it was a nightmare to find information and things only got settled last minute both in Copenhagen and in Budapest even though I followed all deadlines.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received no assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. I booked housing 6 months before arrival so I found a good place.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I booked through spotahome who works with Erasmus and I can recommend that.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The registration system is a nightmare for Erasmus students. There is no space left even though they tell you there is.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to write individual emails to each lecturer plus the responsible lecturer AND show up at each lecture/class that we wished to join and ask to be accepted, so the first 5 weeks was extremely stressful not knowing which subjects to attend.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: No help was available.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very succesful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Hope for the best.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The classes and lectures were interesting, inspiring, focused on practice and the lecturers were very competent.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was good/high and the lecturers were passionate and inspiring.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching at ELTE is focused on how to use the knowledge in practice, so all theory is linked to "real life" examples in both research fields and clinical situations and how to apply the theory in pravctice, which is very different and more useful than the super theoretical approach in UCPH, which mostly focuses on being good at studying and understanding the theory.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
I was enrolled in 8 courses, but should have been enrolled in 11 to be able to transfer all 30 credits.
Clinical interviewing skills
Academic writing and presentation skills.
Introduction to counselling psychology.
Introduction to bordering sciences.
Culture and society.
Psychological ethics and legal issues.
Observation and field research.
Interview, content analysis and focus group.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The Psychological Ethics and legal issues was SUPER interesting and extremely useful and important when working in any field of psychology. I definitely recommend it!
I also recommend taking Basic clinical interviewing skills and Introductio to counselling psychology, because you get very important tools to create safe therapy spaces for clients.

questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I found it challenging to work in groups with the other students because our approaches and backgrounds were so different.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The diversity is amazingly inspirering.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be prepared for a big mess in the registration system.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have patience and trust that it will work out and allow yourself to relax as much as you need, because the amount of pressure can be rough.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Dance classes in my free time.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The whole administration process from the first application in UCPH, all the steps during the preparations before the exchange, the registration and not knowing if the international office in Denmark would approve my courses and not knowing if the Erasmus Grant would be cut in half or not.
